newsitem.title: LEBANON: Hizbollah no comment on missing Israeli airman.
newsitem.headline: Hizbollah no comment on missing Israeli airman.

text.p: The pro-Iranian Hizbollah declined to comment on Sunday on a Beirut newspaper report that it had made progress in tracing missing Israeli airman Ron Arad who was shot down over Lebanon in 1986.
"We do not have anything to say on this subject," a Hizbollah (Party of God) spokesman told Reuters by telephone.
As-Sharq daily said German security official Bernd Schmidbauer was involved in a planned exchange deal but officials at the German embassy in Beirut could not be contacted for comment.

As-Sharq quoted unidentified sources on Saturday as saying Germany was helping to prepare a top secret deal to exchange Arad for Hizbollah cleric Sheikh Abdel Karim Obeid and Islamist faction leader Mustapha Dirani and other Lebanese and Palestinians held in Israeli jails.
Germany helped negotiate a big exchange in July of prisoners and bodies between Hizbollah and Israel and its militia ally.

As-Sharq's editor Awni Kaaki is close to Syrian leaders whose 35,000 troops in Lebanon make Syria the country's main powerbrokers, but the daily is known more for its society pages and relatively daring pin-ups than for reporting developments in major political stories.

"Well informed sources told As-Sharq that the German security official who sponsored the previous deal between Israel and Hizbollah to exchange the bodies of dead Israeli soldiers for some Lebanese detainees and dead Hizbollah members held in Israel is behind the effort to exchange Arad for Sheikh Obeid, Dirani and other Lebanese and Palestinian detainees in Israeli prisons," the newspaper said.
"According to some indications in the last two days, information given to the German government indicated that Hizbollah's efforts to locate Arad achieved some positive results," it said.

"The German security official is expected to come to Lebanon and Israel soon to achieve the deal on exchanging Arad for Sheikh Obeid, Dirani and other Lebanese and Palestinian prisoners in Israeli jails," it added.
Schmidbauer negotiated an exchange in July between Hizbollah and Israel and its militia ally in south Lebanon, the South Lebanon Army (SLA).

Under the deal, Israel handed back the remains of 123 dead Hizbollah fighters and the SLA freed 45 prisoners in exchange for the remains of Israeli soldiers Yossi Fink and Rahamim Alsheikh, which had been held for more than a decade, and 17 SLA captives released by Hizbollah.

Hizbollah has said Arad was captured after his plane was shot down but it does not know if he is now alive or dead. Schmidbauer said in July it seemed clear he was alive in 1990 but his movements after that were unclear.
